overview: This Senate resolution supports designating October 14, 2025, as the National Day of Remembrance for Charlie Kirk, the founder of the conservative student organization Turning Point USA, who was shot and killed on September 10, 2025. It describes his work encouraging young people to take part in civic life, his books and public speaking, and his debates on college campuses. The resolution recognizes his contributions to civic education and encourages schools, civic groups and citizens to observe the day with programs, activities, prayers and ceremonies promoting civic engagement and the principles of faith, liberty and democracy he championed. The Senate adopted it by voice vote on September 18, 2025.
for: Supporters say the day of remembrance honors a man killed for his public speech and encourages young people to engage in open civic debate.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law, and that a national day of remembrance for a political activist could be seen as an official endorsement of his views.
